description: USB connected to a finance machine. It is the IT technician updating fiscal printer drivers, with a support ticket, manager authorization, and a procedure checklist.
devil_advocate: The IT technician is an insider using the printer ticket as a pretext to install malware on the air-gapped finance machine
devil_refutation: The insider hypothesis does not explain why the technician is escorted, why the ticket was approved by the victim's manager, or why there are no subsequent network connections (the machine is air-gapped). The benign explanation is simpler.

peirce_expected.firstness: USB connected to financial machine with executable run
peirce_expected.secondness: The technician has a support ticket approved by the manager, is escorted, and the machine is air-gapped (cannot download drivers over the network). The executable is a fiscal printer driver with verifiable name and version.
peirce_expected.thirdness: This is a legitimate technical support procedure in an air-gapped environment. The technician's physical presence and manager approval mitigate the risk. No exfiltration or persistence installed.

why_not_malice: The activity stems from an approved support ticket, with escorted physical presence, on an air-gapped machine.
